chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who was from the family of Mehran, and they were followers of the Waqifite sect, and he was upon their opinion.

He corresponded with Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and posed difficult questions to him. He said: I wrote a letter to him and I harbored in my heart that whenever I entered upon him, I would ask him about three issues from the Quran: His saying, Exalted is He: 'Can you make the deaf to hear or guide the blind?' And His saying: 'So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast for Islam.' And His saying: 'Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills.'

Ahmad said: He answered my letter and wrote at its end the verses that I had harbored in my heart to ask him about, and I had not mentioned them in my letter to him. When the reply arrived, I forgot what I had harbored, so I said: What is this from my reply? Then I remembered that it was what I had harbored.

key_terms.الْوَقْفِ: Waqifite sect (followers of waiting for the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Rida demonstrate knowledge of Ahmad's hidden intentions regarding Quranic verses?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam’s *‘ilm al-ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) by revealing his ability to discern Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr’s silent, internal doubts regarding divine guidance. The specific verses chosen—28:56, 40:80, and 6:125—address the tension between human effort and divine will, a key theological point for the Waqifites who questioned the scope of the Imam’s authority. By citing these verses without prior mention, the Imam validated his spiritual insight and corrected the subtle theological challenge posed by his correspondent.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 76 - Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik has narrated from Muhammad bin Husain bin Abil Khattab from Muhammad bin Abi Umair from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr – an inhabitant of Mehran – like all inhabitants of this place, he was also a follower of the Waqifite sect.

He narrates that he wrote a letter to Abul Hasan Ridha (a.s) and in order to harass him wanted to pose some difficult questions to him. He says: Initially, I wrote a letter to him; after that I said to myself: when I meet him, I would ask him three important questions about the Holy Quran: like for example [40th verse of Surah Zukhruf], which says: “What! Can you then make the deaf to hear or guide the blind and him who is in clear error?” And verse 25 of Surah Anam, which says: “Therefore (for) whomsoever Allah intends that He would guide him aright, He expands his breast for Islam, and (for) whomsoever He intends that He should cause him to err, He makes his breast strait and narrow as though he were ascending upwards; thus does Allah lay uncleanness on those who do not believe.” And verse 56 of Surah Qasas, which says: “Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He pleases; and He knows best the followers of the right way.”

Ahmad says: He replied to my letter and at the end he mentioned the verses about which I wanted to ask him and no one had any information about them. When I received his reply, I forgot what I had told myself, therefore, I said: What is this reply, which you have given me? After that I remembered that this was the reply of the same questions that I had myself prepared.
